newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Australia recalls Knox for Springbok test.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Australia recalls Knox for Springbok test.

text.p: Australia have recalled veteran fly-half David Knox to their squad for this weekend's Tri-Nations test against South Africa after a remarkable change of mind by coach Greg Smith.

Knox will interrupt a stint with South African province Natal to join the Wallabies in Brisbane for Saturday's test as a replacement for injured Tim Horan, an Australian Rugby Union spokesman said on Monday.
Smith has persistently overlooked Knox this season, preferring to switch Horan from centre despite a near-total lack of previous experience in the specialist fly-half position.

Horan broke his hand during the first half of Australia's 33-18 defeat against New Zealand in the Tri-Nations test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday and will be out of action for six to eight weeks.
In justiying his selection decisions, Smith has repeatedly argued that Knox's acknowledged talent as an attacking force does not compensate for his poor defensive ability.
Those offensive skills helped ACT Brumbies reach the Super 12 final in March, when they lost to holders Auckland. His performances subsequently earned praise from All Black coach John Hart.
When Smith opted for Horan for earlier home test matches against France, Knox signed to play Natal in the domestic Currie Cup competition.
Knox, who launched a scathing attack on Australia's selection policy before his departurne, will leave South Africa late on Monday night, according to the ARU spokesman.
Queensland fly-half Elton Flatley has also been called up into the squad, the spokesman said.
